In this world, every promise is a string. Wrist to wrist. Break it, and it snaps. And you can never tie it back.
You'll come to my recital? Promise?
At six, his meeting runs late. The string gets thinner by the minute.
It doesn't tie. I already tried.
The next week, he doesn't promise anything. He just comes. An hour early.
I didn't want to break another one.
Then I'll promise. I'll look for you.
